newsitem.title: USA: US to make strong efforts at Japan insurance pact.
newsitem.headline: US to make strong efforts at Japan insurance pact.

text.p: The United States will make "strong efforts" to resolve a long-simmering dispute with Japan over insurance during trade talks in San Francisco, a U.S. trade official said on Friday.

"The United States is entering into these talks with the intention of making strong efforts to reach a resolution and we intend to work hard towards that goal," the U.S. official told Reuters. He spoke on the condition he not be identified.
Senior U.S. and Japanese trade negotiators here are set to start this latest round of talks later Friday and Saturday in hopes of resolving the dispute over access to Japan's market.

The United States wants Japan to live up to a 1994 agreement that calls for deregulation of the primary sector dominated by big Japanese firms before deregulation of the so-called third sector of specialty insurance, which is dominated by foreign companies.
On Thursday, a U.S. trade official in Washington expressed doubt that the dispute would be fully resolved in the upcoming round of talks.
The U.S. official said the "ball is substantially in Japan's court" at the upcoming talks because Tokyo removed a number of primary sector issues from the table during negotiations in September.
Little progress can be made if those issues are not returned to the table, the official said.
Earlier, a senior Japanese Financial Ministry official told reporters in San Francisco that Japan is seeking a way to resolve differences with the U.S. during the talks.
Japan's domestic insurance market is valued at about $382 billion.
